purpose: Skeleton-first hindfoot/midfoot audit. Determine what can and cannot be inferred from the a003 tarsal control sticks, and define the anatomical rebuild requirement.
findings: The a003 tarsal control-stick lengths are not internally interpretable as whole-bone lengths: for example the calcaneus stick is ~19 mm while adult male CT axial calcaneal length is ~75 mm, whereas the cuboid stick is ~52 mm while dry-bone cuboid length averages ~34 mm.
This mismatch does not mean the joint positions are automatically wrong; it proves the current tarsal Blender bones are schematic control/reference segments rather than anatomical bone geometry.

The canonical skeleton therefore cannot freeze the tarsus by validating stick length alone. Each tarsal needs a distinct anatomical centre, principal axis, proximal/distal contact landmarks and bone-envelope dimensions stored separately from the control segment.

Independent sources agree on the whole-tarsus size hierarchy: calcaneus largest, talus second; cuboid/navicular/medial cuneiform intermediate; lateral/intermediate cuneiform smaller. The canonical representation must preserve this hierarchy in its bone envelopes.

Because the current foot surface and metatarsal/toe chains are oversized, hindfoot/midfoot centres must be rebuilt before the final foot mesh is shortened; otherwise the correction could be concentrated incorrectly in the toes or forefoot.
required_canonical_fields_per_tarsal: principal long axis and secondary axes
whole-bone length/width/height or equivalent envelope dimensions
functional joint-centre offsets from the bone centroid
source and measurement definition for every numerical value
acceptance_tests: No tarsal may be accepted solely because its Blender stick length is plausible.
Whole-bone envelope hierarchy must agree with source evidence.
Talocrural, subtalar, talonavicular, calcaneocuboid and TMT contact centres must remain distinct.
Neutral axes and joint motion must remain anatomically coherent after the foot is shortened.
The final heel-to-toe mesh length must arise from the canonical hindfoot + midfoot + forefoot chain plus explicit soft-tissue allowances.
